name: Question 17
problem:
A particular shop sells chickens and turkeys. The weight of a chicken is normally distributed with a mean of $1.5\,\text{kg}$ and a standard deviation of $0.1\,\text{kg}.$ The weight of a turkey is normally distributed with a mean of $8\,\text{kg}$ and a standard deviation of $0.4\,\text{kg}.$ If a chicken and a turkey are randomly selected, what is the probability that $5$ times the weight of the chicken is greater than the turkey's weight? You may assume that the weights are independent. 

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7734\,$ | $\,0.7764\,$ | $\,0.7794\,$ | $\,0.7823\,$ | $\,0.7852\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.8023\,$ | $\,0.8051\,$ | $\,0.8078\,$ | $\,0.8106\,$ | $\,0.8133\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8289\,$ | $\,0.8315\,$ | $\,0.8340\,$ | $\,0.8365\,$ | $\,0.8389\,$ |
worked_solution:
Let $X$ denote the weight of a chicken, and let $Y$ denote the weight of a turkey. We want to find 

$$
P(5X>Y)=P(5X-Y>0).
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables such that $X∼N(1.5,{0.1}^{2})$ and $Y∼N(8,{0.4}^{2}),$ then 

$$
\begin{aligned}5X-Y & ∼N(5\cdot 1.5-8,{5}^{2}\cdot {0.1}^{2}+{0.4}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(-0.5,0.41).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variable $5X-Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =-0.5$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{0.41}.$

To find $P(5X-Y>0),$ we convert $5X-Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(5X-Y>0) & =P(Z>\frac{0-(-0.5)}{\sqrt{0.41}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>0.78) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.78) \\  & =1-Φ(0.78)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.78)≈0.7823.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(5X-Y>0) & ≈1-Φ(0.78) \\  & ≈1-0.7823 \\  & 0.2177.\end{aligned}
$$
